reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard binary package that downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub releases (github.com/0sec-labs/foxguard) with SHA256 checksums pinned. There is no top-level code execution during sourcing, the latestver() helper is defined but never invoked during build/install, and the package() function performs only standard file installation. The .SRCINFO contains matching pinned metadata. No injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not substantive: qwen3-235b returned 'inconclusive' solely because its LLM API request for .SRCINFO failed with HTTP 400 (BadRequestError), not because of any security concern. The model's actual analysis of the PKGBUILD correctly identified it as safe. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed both files and returned 'safe' with accurate reasoning. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only and also concluded safe.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to audit .SRCINFO due to LLM API error (HTTP 400), resulting in an inconclusive overall verdict despite correctly analyzing the PKGBUILD
learnings: When a model returns 'inconclusive' due to a tool/API error rather than a substantive security finding, the audit system should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to analysis uncertainty' and 'inconclusive due to infrastructure failure' — the latter should not block a verdict when other models successfully completed the review
For -bin packages with only PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, models correctly identify that there is no additional source code or install hooks to review; file selection logic is working as intended

The latestver() helper pattern (curl + sed to fetch version metadata from GitHub API) is correctly recognized by all models as non-executed during build — this common AUR pattern should remain excluded from injection concerns
